# MexR and NalD are pyocyanin-responsive transcriptional repressors of the efflux pump MexAB-OprM in Pseudomonas aeruginosa ## ABSTRACT The secondary metabolite pyocyanin (PYO) significantly enhances the antibiotic resistance of Pseudomonas aeruginosa by inducing expression of the resistance-nodulation-cell division efflux systems.
MexR and NalD, the primary repressors, form a dimer and bind to the distal and proximal promoters of the MexAB-OprM operon, respectively.
MexR and NalD are the two most important repressors of MexAB-OprM, and mutations in mexR and nalD frequently occur in clinically isolated strains of P. aeruginosa [36, 37].
In this study, we demonstrate that PYO positively regulates the MexAB-OprM efflux pump by directly binding to and inhibiting its transcriptional repressors, MexR and NalD.
